answer: A kernel escrow tells a real agent from copies. Each identity locks 120 credits and records a kernel of cadence and client mix. A prism check each epoch refracts new behavior into work and client facets; drift freezes the escrow, and a third unlocks after a clean epoch. The horizon is three epochs: full release needs three matches. The kth fake needs its own kernel and 120 credits, so 1000 fakes lock 120000 with no bulk discount, while one honest agent pays 120 once. Rented behavior fails: a shared stream carries one jitter fingerprint, freezing every identity fed by it.
